<domain_knowledge>
- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
I want to understand how the recommendation position influences user clicks. Could you return the position, total recommendations, total clicks, and recommendation click-through rate (RCTR) for each position. Sort the results by position in ascending order.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Recommendation Position Illustration: Depicts the effect of recommendation placement on user visibility and engagement.
  Definition: A recommendation placed in position 3, for example, may benefit from higher prominence compared to lower-ranked placements.
- Recommendation Click-Through Rate (RCTR): Defines RCTR as the ratio of clicks to total recommendations.
  Definition: RCTR = (clicks / recommendations) when recommendations are greater than zero.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT
    r.posval AS position,
    COUNT(DISTINCT r.reckey) AS total_recommendations,
    COUNT(i.intkey) AS total_clicks,
    CAST(COUNT(i.intkey) AS REAL) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT r.reckey), 0) AS rctr
FROM recommendations r
LEFT JOIN interactions i
    ON i.reclink = r.reckey
    AND TRIM(i.evttype) = 'click'
    AND COALESCE(TRIM(i.clktype), '') <> ''
    AND COALESCE(TRIM(i.clksrc), '') <> ''
    AND COALESCE(TRIM(i.clkctx), '') <> ''
GROUP BY r.posval
ORDER BY r.posval;

<domain_knowledge>
- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- Click-through rate (CTR): Fraction of page views that result in a click. Selects 5% of rows.
  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
</domain_knowledge>

<domain_knowledge>
- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- Click-through rate (CTR): Fraction of page views that result in a click. Selects 5% of rows.
  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
Develop a direct calculation method for the Recommendation Relevance Score (RRS) that computes the average of recscore, confval, and recutil values using the formula (recscore + confval + recutil) / 3. Since SQLite doesn't support custom functions, implement this as an inline calculation that can be used directly in SELECT statements or create a view if needed for reusable RRS calculations across the recommendations data.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Recommendation Relevance Score (RRS): Computes the overall relevance of a recommendation by averaging recommendation score, algorithm confidence, and utility.
  Definition: RRS = ((recscore + confval + recutil)) / (3), where the contributing factors capture recommendation performance.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS rrs AS
SELECT r.reckey,
       (r.recscore + r.confval + s.recutil) / 3.0 AS rrs
FROM recommendations r
JOIN interactions i ON r.reckey = i.reclink
JOIN sessions s ON i.seshlink2 = s.seshkey;

instances.question:
We need to set up automatic logging for user activity to supports the Interaction Timeliness Indicator (ITI). Could you create a trigger that will automatically create a corresponding default record (intmetkey, interaction_behavior) in the 'interactionmetrics' table whenever a new interaction is logged? Use 'Interaction Default Values' for the JSON structure 'interaction_behavior' with appropriate initial values.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Interaction Timeliness Indicator (ITI): Evaluates the promptness of user interactions after content presentation.
  Definition: A minimal delay between content exposure and user interaction indicates high interest, thereby enhancing content performance metrics.
- Interaction Default Values: A standardized set of initial values assigned to interaction behavior metrics when a new interaction record is created.
  Definition: A JSON structure: jsonb_build_object('scroll', jsonb_build_object('depth', 0, 'speed', 0.0, 'percentage', 0), 'exit_type', 'Natural', 'conversion', jsonb_build_object('value', 0, 'status', 'None'), 'time_spent', jsonb_build_object('viewport_time', 0, 'attention_time', 0, 'reading_seconds', 0, 'duration_seconds', 0), 'next_action', 'None', 'bounce_status', 'No', 'click_seconds', 0)
- Content Interaction Efficiency (CIE): Measures how efficiently a user interacts with content inside a session by looking at the average relative order in which events occur (their sequence values)
  Definition: CIE = AVG(seqval)

Here `seqval` is the event’s sequence/position within a session (e.g., 1, 2, 3…).  Average it across all interactions in a session.
</definitions>

<domain_knowledge>
- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- Click-through rate (CTR): Fraction of page views that result in a click. Selects 5% of rows.
  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
We need to set up automatic logging for user activity to supports the Interaction Timeliness Indicator (ITI). Could you create a trigger that will automatically create a corresponding default record (intmetkey, interaction_behavior) in the 'interactionmetrics' table whenever a new interaction is logged? Use 'Interaction Default Values' for the JSON structure 'interaction_behavior' with appropriate initial values.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Interaction Timeliness Indicator (ITI): Evaluates the promptness of user interactions after content presentation.
  Definition: A minimal delay between content exposure and user interaction indicates high interest, thereby enhancing content performance metrics.
- Interaction Default Values: A standardized set of initial values assigned to interaction behavior metrics when a new interaction record is created.
  Definition: A JSON structure: jsonb_build_object('scroll', jsonb_build_object('depth', 0, 'speed', 0.0, 'percentage', 0), 'exit_type', 'Natural', 'conversion', jsonb_build_object('value', 0, 'status', 'None'), 'time_spent', jsonb_build_object('viewport_time', 0, 'attention_time', 0, 'reading_seconds', 0, 'duration_seconds', 0), 'next_action', 'None', 'bounce_status', 'No', 'click_seconds', 0)
- Content Interaction Efficiency (CIE): Measures how efficiently a user interacts with content inside a session by looking at the average relative order in which events occur (their sequence values)
  Definition: CIE = AVG(seqval)

Here `seqval` is the event’s sequence/position within a session (e.g., 1, 2, 3…).  Average it across all interactions in a session.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS interaction_default_values_trigger
AFTER INSERT ON interactions
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO interactionmetrics (intmetkey, interaction_behavior)
    VALUES (
        NEW.intkey,
        json_object(
            'scroll', json_object('depth', 0, 'speed', 0.0, 'percentage', 0),
            'exit_type', 'Natural',
            'conversion', json_object('value', 0, 'status', 'None'),
            'time_spent', json_object('viewport_time', 0, 'attention_time', 0, 'reading_seconds', 0, 'duration_seconds', 0),
            'next_action', 'None',
            'bounce_status', 'No',
            'click_seconds', 0
        )
    );
END;

<domain_knowledge>
- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- Click-through rate (CTR): Fraction of page views that result in a click. Selects 5% of rows.
  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
</domain_knowledge>

- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- Click-through rate (CTR): Fraction of page views that result in a click. Selects 5% of rows.
  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
Show me the equipment type, equipment code, Equipment Efficiency Rating, safety index, efficiency rank, safety rank, and the absolute rank difference between them. Sort the results by equipment type and then by EER in descending order.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Equipment Efficiency Rating (EER): A composite metric that evaluates the overall efficiency of equipment based on performance, reliability, and environmental impact.
  Definition: EER = (performanceindex + reliabilityindex) / (2) * (1 - (environmentalimpactindex) / (10)), where higher values indicate more efficient equipment with better performance and lower environmental impact.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH equipment_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    e.equipmenttype,
    e.equipmentcode,
    e.safetyindex,
    ((e.performanceindex + e.reliabilityindex) / 2.0) * (1 - (CAST(e.environmentalimpactindex AS REAL) / 10.0)) AS equipment_efficiency_rating
  FROM equipment e
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    em.equipmenttype,
    em.equipmentcode,
    em.safetyindex,
    em.equipment_efficiency_rating,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY em.equipment_efficiency_rating DESC) AS efficiency_rank,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY em.safetyindex DESC) AS safety_rank
  FROM equipment_metrics em
)
SELECT
  r.equipmenttype,
  r.equipmentcode,
  r.equipment_efficiency_rating,
  r.safetyindex,
  r.efficiency_rank,
  r.safety_rank,
  ABS(r.efficiency_rank - r.safety_rank) AS absolute_rank_difference
FROM ranked r
ORDER BY r.equipmenttype ASC, r.equipment_efficiency_rating DESC;

For each chassis in our database, calculate the Vehicle Performance Coefficient. I need a report showing the chassis registry ID first, followed by the calculated VPC value. Please include all chassis records in your analysis, even those without corresponding engine data.

  Definition: VPC = (1 - (brakepadwearpercent + trackwearpercent) / (200)) * (vehiclespeedkmh) / (50) * (engineloadpercent) / (100), where lower wear percentages and optimal engine load contribute to better performance.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT c.chassisregistry,
       (1.0 - (CAST(c.brakepadwearpercent AS REAL) + CAST(c.trackwearpercent AS REAL)) / NULLIF(200.0, 0)) *

FROM chassisandvehicle c

instances.question:
Could you identify all equipment that meets the Extreme Weather Readiness criteria in our polar database? Show me the equipment code, equipment type, heater status, insulation status, emergency light status, the calculated Structural Safety Factor, and the Extreme Weather Readiness Status. Make sure to include all equipment with available structural safety data, even if some equipment might be missing cabin environment, lighting safety, or thermal insulation information.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Extreme Weather Readiness (EWR): Evaluates how prepared equipment and structures are for extreme weather conditions.
  Definition: A composite rating where equipment is considered 'Extreme Weather Ready' if it maintains an SSF > 0.7 and has operational heating systems (heaterstatus not 'Off'), proper insulation (insulationstatus not 'Poor'), and functional emergency systems (emergencylightstatus = 'On' or 'Testing').
- Extreme Weather Readiness Status (EWRS): A binary classification system that determines if equipment has met all necessary conditions to safely operate during extreme weather events.
  Definition: Equipment is classified as 'Extreme Weather Ready' WHEN (SSF > 0.7) AND (heaterstatus != 'Off') AND (insulationstatus != 'Poor') AND (emergencylightstatus IN ('On', 'Testing')); OTHERWISE equipment is classified as 'Not Ready'. This evaluation combines structural integrity checks with essential operational systems status to determine immediate readiness for extreme weather exposure.
- Structural Safety Factor (SSF): Evaluates the safety margin of structures under extreme weather conditions.
  Definition: SSF = (100 - structuralloadpercent) / (100) * CASE WHEN snowloadkgm2 > 100 or windspeedms > 20 THEN 0.5 WHEN snowloadkgm2 > 50 or windspeedms > 10 THEN 0.8 ELSE 1.0 END
</definitions>

<domain_knowledge>
- snowloadkgm2: Snow load in kg/m2 approximated as 10 kg/m2 for each centimeter of snow depth.
  Measured: snowloadkgm2 does not hold snowdepthcm * 10 in this database
- structuralloadpercent: Structural load as a percentage of a 1000 kg/m2 rated capacity.
  Measured: structuralloadpercent does not hold (snowloadkgm2 * 100) / 1000 in this database
- Scientific equipment ready for measurement (SERM): Scientific equipment is operating, logging data, with normal sensors and valid calibration. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: scientificequipmentstatus = 'Operating' AND dataloggingstatus = 'Active' AND sensorstatus = 'Normal' AND calibrationstatus = 'Valid'
- Generation-to-load power ratio (GLR): Total wind, solar, and fuel-cell generation per watt of battery consumption.
  Definition: (thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.wind.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.solar.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.fuelcelloutputw) / powerbattery.powerconsumptionw
- Solar panel fault at Antarctic station (SPFAS): Solar panel fault occurring on equipment located in Antarctica.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.solarpanelstatus) = 'Fault' AND TRIM(location.locationtype) = 'Antarctic'
- Wind turbine fault at high altitude (WTFHA): Wind turbine fault recorded on equipment located above 3000 meters.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.windturbinestatus) = 'Fault' AND location.altitudem > 3000
- Active logging with high latency: Active data logging on equipment with latency above 1000 milliseconds.
  Definition: TRIM(scientific.dataloggingstatus) = 'Active' AND communication.json_extract(signalmetrics, '$.latency_ms') > 1000
- Failed communication equipment inspection: Communication equipment whose inspection result is Failed.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.inspectionstatus) = 'Failed' AND TRIM(equipment.equipmenttype) = 'Communication'
- Non-compliant equipment with high engine temperature: Non-compliant equipment with engine temperature above 130 degrees Celsius.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.compliancestatus) = 'Non-compliant' AND engineandfluids.enginetemperaturec > 130
- Active equipment with antenna error: Active equipment whose communication antenna is in Error state.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.operationalstatus) = 'Active' AND TRIM(communication.antennastatus) = 'Error'
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
Could you identify all equipment that meets the Extreme Weather Readiness criteria in our polar database? Show me the equipment code, equipment type, heater status, insulation status, emergency light status, the calculated Structural Safety Factor, and the Extreme Weather Readiness Status. Make sure to include all equipment with available structural safety data, even if some equipment might be missing cabin environment, lighting safety, or thermal insulation information.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Extreme Weather Readiness (EWR): Evaluates how prepared equipment and structures are for extreme weather conditions.
  Definition: A composite rating where equipment is considered 'Extreme Weather Ready' if it maintains an SSF > 0.7 and has operational heating systems (heaterstatus not 'Off'), proper insulation (insulationstatus not 'Poor'), and functional emergency systems (emergencylightstatus = 'On' or 'Testing').
- Extreme Weather Readiness Status (EWRS): A binary classification system that determines if equipment has met all necessary conditions to safely operate during extreme weather events.
  Definition: Equipment is classified as 'Extreme Weather Ready' WHEN (SSF > 0.7) AND (heaterstatus != 'Off') AND (insulationstatus != 'Poor') AND (emergencylightstatus IN ('On', 'Testing')); OTHERWISE equipment is classified as 'Not Ready'. This evaluation combines structural integrity checks with essential operational systems status to determine immediate readiness for extreme weather exposure.
- Structural Safety Factor (SSF): Evaluates the safety margin of structures under extreme weather conditions.
  Definition: SSF = (100 - structuralloadpercent) / (100) * CASE WHEN snowloadkgm2 > 100 or windspeedms > 20 THEN 0.5 WHEN snowloadkgm2 > 50 or windspeedms > 10 THEN 0.8 ELSE 1.0 END
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

```sql
WITH structural AS (
  SELECT
    eq.equipmentcode,
    eq.equipmenttype,
    ce.heaterstatus,
    ts.insulationstatus,
    ls.emergencylightstatus,
    (CAST(100 - w.structuralloadpercent AS REAL) / 100.0) *
      (CASE
        WHEN w.snowloadkgm2 > 100 OR w.windspeedms > 20 THEN 0.5
        WHEN w.snowloadkgm2 > 50 OR w.windspeedms > 10 THEN 0.8
        ELSE 1.0
       END) AS structural_safety_factor
  FROM weatherandstructure w
  JOIN location loc ON w.weatherlocref = loc.locationregistry
  JOIN equipment eq ON loc.loceqref = eq.equipmentcode
  LEFT JOIN cabinenvironment ce ON eq.equipmentcode = ce.cabineqref
  LEFT JOIN thermalsolarwindandgrid ts ON eq.equipmentcode = ts.thermaleqref
  LEFT JOIN lightingandsafety ls ON eq.equipmentcode = ls.lighteqref
  WHERE w.structuralloadpercent IS NOT NULL
    AND w.snowloadkgm2 IS NOT NULL
    AND w.windspeedms IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  s.equipmentcode,
  s.equipmenttype,
  s.heaterstatus,
  s.insulationstatus,
  s.emergencylightstatus,
  s.structural_safety_factor,
  CASE
    WHEN s.structural_safety_factor > 0.7
      AND s.heaterstatus IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.heaterstatus) <> 'Off'
      AND s.insulationstatus IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.insulationstatus) <> 'Poor'
      AND s.emergencylightstatus IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.emergencylightstatus) IN ('On', 'Testing')
    THEN 'Extreme Weather Ready'
    ELSE 'Not Ready'
  END AS extreme_weather_readiness_status
FROM structural s;
```

For our polar safety assessment, I need to evaluate the safety equipment's Life Support System Reliability. Please provide a report showing the equipment code, equipment type, life support status, calculated LSSR score (rounded to 2 decimal places), and reliability classification based on Life Support Reliability Classification. Also include a JSON summary of oxygen status , medical status, and safety system status as support systems status with fields names: 'oxygen_status', 'medical_status', 'safety_system_status'. Focus only on safety equipment and sort the results by LSSR in descending order.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Operational Readiness Score (ORS): Quantifies how ready equipment is for immediate deployment based on operational status and maintenance schedule.
  Definition: ORS = CASE WHEN operationalstatus = 'Active' THEN 10 * (1 - (operationhours) / (maintenancecyclehours)) WHEN operationalstatus = 'Standby' THEN 5 * (1 - (operationhours) / (maintenancecyclehours)) ELSE 0 END
- Thermal Insulation Efficiency (TIE): Measures how effectively a structure retains heat based on insulation status and heat loss rate.
  Definition: TIE = CASE WHEN insulationstatus = 'Good' THEN 0.9 - (heatlossratekwh) / (10) WHEN insulationstatus = 'Fair' THEN 0.6 - (heatlossratekwh) / (10) WHEN insulationstatus = 'Poor' THEN 0.3 - (heatlossratekwh) / (10) END, where lower heat loss and better insulation result in higher efficiency.
- Life Support System Reliability (LSSR): Evaluates the reliability of life support systems under polar conditions
  Definition: LSSR = 0.7 * ORS + 0.3 * TIE
- Life Support Reliability Classification (LSRC): Categorizes life support systems into reliability classes based on their LSSR score for operational decision-making.
  Definition: Life support systems are classified into three reliability categories: 'High Reliability' WHEN (LSSR >= 0.8), 'Moderate Reliability' WHEN (LSSR >= 0.6 AND LSSR < 0.8), and 'Low Reliability' WHEN (LSSR < 0.6).
</definitions>

          e.equipmenttype,
          ls.lifesupportstatus,
          ls.oxygensupplystatus,
          ls.medicalequipmentstatus,
          ls.safetysystemstatus,
          (0.7 * CASE
                     WHEN TRIM(om.operationalstatus) = 'Active' THEN 10 * (1 - CAST(om.operationhours AS REAL) / NULLIF(om.maintenancecyclehours, 0))
                     WHEN TRIM(om.operationalstatus) = 'Standby' THEN 5 * (1 - CAST(om.operationhours AS REAL) / NULLIF(om.maintenancecyclehours, 0))
                     ELSE 0
                 END + 0.3 * CASE
                                 WHEN TRIM(t.insulationstatus) = 'Good' THEN 0.9 - t.heatlossratekwh / 10.0
                                 WHEN TRIM(t.insulationstatus) = 'Fair' THEN 0.6 - t.heatlossratekwh / 10.0
                                 WHEN TRIM(t.insulationstatus) = 'Poor' THEN 0.3 - t.heatlossratekwh / 10.0
                             END) AS lssr
   FROM equipment e
   JOIN lightingandsafety ls ON e.equipmentcode = ls.lighteqref
   JOIN operationmaintenance om ON e.equipmentcode = om.opmainteqref
   JOIN thermalsolarwindandgrid t ON e.equipmentcode = t.thermaleqref
   WHERE TRIM(e.equipmenttype) = 'Safety')
SELECT equipmentcode,
       equipmenttype,
       lifesupportstatus,
       ROUND(lssr, 2) AS lssr_score,
       CASE
           WHEN lssr >= 0.8 THEN 'High Reliability'
           WHEN lssr >= 0.6 THEN 'Moderate Reliability'
           ELSE 'Low Reliability'
       END AS reliability_classification,
       json_object('oxygen_status', oxygensupplystatus, 'medical_status', medicalequipmentstatus, 'safety_system_status', safetysystemstatus) AS support_systems_status
FROM metrics
ORDER BY lssr DESC;

                                 WHEN TRIM(t.insulationstatus) = 'Poor' THEN 0.3 - t.heatlossratekwh / 10.0
                             END) AS lssr
   FROM equipment e
   JOIN lightingandsafety ls ON e.equipmentcode = ls.lighteqref
   JOIN operationmaintenance om ON e.equipmentcode = om.opmainteqref
   JOIN thermalsolarwindandgrid t ON e.equipmentcode = t.thermaleqref
   WHERE TRIM(e.equipmenttype) = 'Safety')
SELECT equipmentcode,
       equipmenttype,
       lifesupportstatus,
       ROUND(lssr, 2) AS lssr_score,
       CASE
           WHEN lssr >= 0.8 THEN 'High Reliability'
           WHEN lssr >= 0.6 THEN 'Moderate Reliability'
           ELSE 'Low Reliability'
       END AS reliability_classification,
       json_object('oxygen_status', oxygensupplystatus, 'medical_status', medicalequipmentstatus, 'safety_system_status', safetysystemstatus) AS support_systems_status
FROM metrics
ORDER BY lssr DESC;

<task>
For our polar safety assessment, I need to evaluate the safety equipment's Life Support System Reliability. Please provide a report showing the equipment code, equipment type, life support status, calculated LSSR score (rounded to 2 decimal places), and reliability classification based on Life Support Reliability Classification. Also include a JSON summary of oxygen status , medical status, and safety system status as support systems status with fields names: 'oxygen_status', 'medical_status', 'safety_system_status'. Focus only on safety equipment and sort the results by LSSR in descending order.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Operational Readiness Score (ORS): Quantifies how ready equipment is for immediate deployment based on operational status and maintenance schedule.
  Definition: ORS = CASE WHEN operationalstatus = 'Active' THEN 10 * (1 - (operationhours) / (maintenancecyclehours)) WHEN operationalstatus = 'Standby' THEN 5 * (1 - (operationhours) / (maintenancecyclehours)) ELSE 0 END
- Thermal Insulation Efficiency (TIE): Measures how effectively a structure retains heat based on insulation status and heat loss rate.
  Definition: TIE = CASE WHEN insulationstatus = 'Good' THEN 0.9 - (heatlossratekwh) / (10) WHEN insulationstatus = 'Fair' THEN 0.6 - (heatlossratekwh) / (10) WHEN insulationstatus = 'Poor' THEN 0.3 - (heatlossratekwh) / (10) END, where lower heat loss and better insulation result in higher efficiency.
- Life Support System Reliability (LSSR): Evaluates the reliability of life support systems under polar conditions
  Definition: LSSR = 0.7 * ORS + 0.3 * TIE
- Life Support Reliability Classification (LSRC): Categorizes life support systems into reliability classes based on their LSSR score for operational decision-making.
  Definition: Life support systems are classified into three reliability categories: 'High Reliability' WHEN (LSSR >= 0.8), 'Moderate Reliability' WHEN (LSSR >= 0.6 AND LSSR < 0.8), and 'Low Reliability' WHEN (LSSR < 0.6).
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH metrics AS (
    SELECT
        e.equipmentcode,
        e.equipmenttype,
        ls.lifesupportstatus,
        ls.oxygensupplystatus,
        ls.medicalequipmentstatus,
        ls.safetysystemstatus,
        (
            0.7 * CASE
                WHEN TRIM(om.operationalstatus) = 'Active'
                    THEN 10 * (1 - CAST(om.operationhours AS REAL) / NULLIF(om.maintenancecyclehours, 0))
                WHEN TRIM(om.operationalstatus) = 'Standby'
                    THEN 5 * (1 - CAST(om.operationhours AS REAL) / NULLIF(om.maintenancecyclehours, 0))
                ELSE 0
            END
            +
            0.3 * CASE
                WHEN TRIM(t.insulationstatus) = 'Good' THEN 0.9 - t.heatlossratekwh / 10.0
                WHEN TRIM(t.insulationstatus) = 'Fair' THEN 0.6 - t.heatlossratekwh / 10.0
                WHEN TRIM(t.insulationstatus) = 'Poor' THEN 0.3 - t.heatlossratekwh / 10.0
            END
        ) AS lssr
    FROM equipment e
    JOIN lightingandsafety ls ON e.equipmentcode = ls.lighteqref
    JOIN operationmaintenance om ON e.equipmentcode = om.opmainteqref
    JOIN thermalsolarwindandgrid t ON e.equipmentcode = t.thermaleqref
    WHERE TRIM(e.equipmenttype) = 'Safety'
)
SELECT
    equipmentcode,
    equipmenttype,
    lifesupportstatus,
    ROUND(lssr, 2) AS lssr_score,
    CASE
        WHEN lssr >= 0.8 THEN 'High Reliability'
        WHEN lssr >= 0.6 THEN 'Moderate Reliability'
        ELSE 'Low Reliability'
    END AS reliability_classification,
    json_object(
        'oxygen_status', oxygensupplystatus,
        'medical_status', medicalequipmentstatus,
        'safety_system_status', safetysystemstatus
    ) AS support_systems_status
FROM metrics
ORDER BY lssr DESC;

Provide the location type, station name, number of equipment at each station, their Renewable Energy Contribution values (rounded to 2 decimal places), total renewable energy output in watts, and how they're categorized according to the Energy Sustainability Classification System? Only include equipment that has measurable solar or wind output data, and sort the results from highest to lowest REC value.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Renewable Energy Contribution (REC): Calculates the percentage contribution of renewable energy sources to the total power generation.
  Definition: REC = (renewablemetrics.solar.output_w + renewablemetrics.wind.output_w) / (fuelcelloutputw + renewablemetrics.solar.output_w + renewablemetrics.wind.output_w) * 100, where higher values indicate greater reliance on renewable energy.
- Energy Sustainability Classification System (ESCS): A comprehensive classification system that categorizes operational energy sustainability based on renewable energy contribution percentages.
  Definition: Operations are classified into three sustainability levels: 'Energy-Sustainable' WHEN (REC > 70); 'Moderately Sustainable' WHEN (REC > 50 AND REC <= 70); 'Low Sustainability' WHEN (REC <= 50).
- Sustainable Energy Operation: Defines the conditions for energy-sustainable operations in polar environments.
  Definition: An operation is considered 'Energy-Sustainable' when it maintains a REC above 70% (meaning more than 70% of energy comes from renewable sources) while maintaining full operational capability and adequate power reserves for at least 48 hours in case of emergency.
</definitions>

<domain_knowledge>
- Scientific equipment ready for measurement (SERM): Scientific equipment is operating, logging data, with normal sensors and valid calibration. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: scientificequipmentstatus = 'Operating' AND dataloggingstatus = 'Active' AND sensorstatus = 'Normal' AND calibrationstatus = 'Valid'
- Generation-to-load power ratio (GLR): Total wind, solar, and fuel-cell generation per watt of battery consumption.
  Definition: (thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.wind.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.solar.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.fuelcelloutputw) / powerbattery.powerconsumptionw
- Solar panel fault at Antarctic station (SPFAS): Solar panel fault occurring on equipment located in Antarctica.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.solarpanelstatus) = 'Fault' AND TRIM(location.locationtype) = 'Antarctic'
- Wind turbine fault at high altitude (WTFHA): Wind turbine fault recorded on equipment located above 3000 meters.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.windturbinestatus) = 'Fault' AND location.altitudem > 3000
- Active logging with high latency: Active data logging on equipment with latency above 1000 milliseconds.
  Definition: TRIM(scientific.dataloggingstatus) = 'Active' AND communication.json_extract(signalmetrics, '$.latency_ms') > 1000
- Failed communication equipment inspection: Communication equipment whose inspection result is Failed.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.inspectionstatus) = 'Failed' AND TRIM(equipment.equipmenttype) = 'Communication'
- Non-compliant equipment with high engine temperature: Non-compliant equipment with engine temperature above 130 degrees Celsius.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.compliancestatus) = 'Non-compliant' AND engineandfluids.enginetemperaturec > 130
- Active equipment with antenna error: Active equipment whose communication antenna is in Error state.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.operationalstatus) = 'Active' AND TRIM(communication.antennastatus) = 'Error'
- Power-to-load ratio (PLR): Battery power draw per kilogram of vehicle load.
  Definition: powerbattery.powerconsumptionw / chassisandvehicle.vehicleloadkg
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
Provide the location type, station name, number of equipment at each station, their Renewable Energy Contribution values (rounded to 2 decimal places), total renewable energy output in watts, and how they're categorized according to the Energy Sustainability Classification System? Only include equipment that has measurable solar or wind output data, and sort the results from highest to lowest REC value.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Renewable Energy Contribution (REC): Calculates the percentage contribution of renewable energy sources to the total power generation.
  Definition: REC = (renewablemetrics.solar.output_w + renewablemetrics.wind.output_w) / (fuelcelloutputw + renewablemetrics.solar.output_w + renewablemetrics.wind.output_w) * 100, where higher values indicate greater reliance on renewable energy.
- Energy Sustainability Classification System (ESCS): A comprehensive classification system that categorizes operational energy sustainability based on renewable energy contribution percentages.
  Definition: Operations are classified into three sustainability levels: 'Energy-Sustainable' WHEN (REC > 70); 'Moderately Sustainable' WHEN (REC > 50 AND REC <= 70); 'Low Sustainability' WHEN (REC <= 50).
- Sustainable Energy Operation: Defines the conditions for energy-sustainable operations in polar environments.
  Definition: An operation is considered 'Energy-Sustainable' when it maintains a REC above 70% (meaning more than 70% of energy comes from renewable sources) while maintaining full operational capability and adequate power reserves for at least 48 hours in case of emergency.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH renewable_equipment AS (
  SELECT
    l.locationtype AS location_type,
    l.stationname AS station_name,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY l.stationname) AS number_of_equipment,
    COALESCE(json_extract(t.renewablemetrics, '$.solar.output_w'), 0)
      + COALESCE(json_extract(t.renewablemetrics, '$.wind.output_w'), 0) AS renewable_output,
    t.fuelcelloutputw
  FROM thermalsolarwindandgrid t
  JOIN location l ON l.loceqref = t.thermaleqref
  WHERE COALESCE(json_extract(t.renewablemetrics, '$.solar.output_w'), 0) > 0
     OR COALESCE(json_extract(t.renewablemetrics, '$.wind.output_w'), 0) > 0
),
rec_calc AS (
  SELECT
    location_type,
    station_name,
    number_of_equipment,
    renewable_output,
    (CAST(renewable_output AS REAL) / NULLIF(renewable_output + fuelcelloutputw, 0)) * 100 AS rec
  FROM renewable_equipment
)
SELECT
  location_type,
  station_name,
  number_of_equipment,
  ROUND(rec, 2) AS renewable_energy_contribution,
  renewable_output AS total_renewable_energy_output_w,
  CASE
    WHEN rec > 70 THEN 'Energy-Sustainable'
    WHEN rec > 50 THEN 'Moderately Sustainable'
    ELSE 'Low Sustainability'
  END AS energy_sustainability_classification
FROM rec_calc
ORDER BY rec DESC;

For each combination of station name and location type, I need to see station names, location types, average water quality indices, average WRMI scores (both rounded to 2 decimal places), count of systems with Water Conservation Requirement, water quality classification, and water resource management status. Sort by highest WRMI first, then by water quality.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Water Resource Management Index (WRMI): Evaluates the efficiency of water resource management based on water levels, quality, and waste levels.
  Definition: WRMI = waterlevelpercent * (waterqualityindex) / (100) * (1 - (wastetanklevelpercent) / (100)), where higher water quality and appropriate water/waste levels indicate better management.
- Water Conservation Requirement: Specifies the conditions under which water conservation measures must be implemented.

<task>
For each combination of station name and location type, I need to see station names, location types, average water quality indices, average WRMI scores (both rounded to 2 decimal places), count of systems with Water Conservation Requirement, water quality classification, and water resource management status. Sort by highest WRMI first, then by water quality.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Water Resource Management Index (WRMI): Evaluates the efficiency of water resource management based on water levels, quality, and waste levels.
  Definition: WRMI = waterlevelpercent * (waterqualityindex) / (100) * (1 - (wastetanklevelpercent) / (100)), where higher water quality and appropriate water/waste levels indicate better management.
- Water Conservation Requirement: Specifies the conditions under which water conservation measures must be implemented.
  Definition: Water conservation measures must be implemented when the WRMI falls below 0.5, indicating either low water levels, poor water quality, or high waste tank levels that require immediate attention to maintain sustainable water usage.
- Water Quality Classification System (WQCS): A standardized system that categorizes water quality for health, safety, and operational purposes in polar environments.
  Definition: Water is classified into five quality categories based on its quality index: 'High-Quality' WHEN (waterqualityindex >= 91), suitable for all purposes including direct consumption; 'Good' WHEN (waterqualityindex >= 71 AND waterqualityindex < 91), safe for consumption after standard treatment; 'Moderate' WHEN (waterqualityindex >= 51 AND waterqualityindex < 71), acceptable for washing but not consumption; 'Poor' WHEN (waterqualityindex >= 26 AND waterqualityindex < 51), suitable only for limited non-contact uses; 'Unsafe' WHEN (waterqualityindex < 26), unsuitable for any use and requiring immediate remediation.
- Water Resource Management Status Classification (WRMSC): A comprehensive classification system that categorizes water resource management status based on WRMI values to guide operational decisions.
  Definition: Water management operations are classified into three status levels: 'Conservation Needed' WHEN (WRMI < 0.5), indicating critical resource limitations requiring immediate conservation measures; 'Monitoring Advised' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.5 AND WRMI < 0.7), representing adequate but vigilant management requiring regular system monitoring; 'Sustainable Management' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.7), indicating optimal water resource utilization suitable for unrestricted operations.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH wrmi_calc AS (
    SELECT
        l.stationname,
        l.locationtype,
        w.waterqualityindex,
        (CAST(w.waterlevelpercent AS REAL) * w.waterqualityindex / 100.0 * (1 - w.wastetanklevelpercent / 100.0)) AS wrmi
    FROM waterandwaste w
    JOIN location l ON w.watereqref = l.loceqref
)
SELECT
    stationname,
    locationtype,
    ROUND(AVG(waterqualityindex), 2) AS average_water_quality_index,
    ROUND(AVG(wrmi), 2) AS average_wrmi,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN wrmi < 0.5 THEN 1 END) AS water_conservation_requirement_count,
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(waterqualityindex) >= 91 THEN 'High-Quality'
        WHEN AVG(waterqualityindex) >= 71 THEN 'Good'
        WHEN AVG(waterqualityindex) >= 51 THEN 'Moderate'
        WHEN AVG(waterqualityindex) >= 26 THEN 'Poor'
        ELSE 'Unsafe'
    END AS water_quality_classification,
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(wrmi) < 0.5 THEN 'Conservation Needed'
        WHEN AVG(wrmi) < 0.7 THEN 'Monitoring Advised'
        ELSE 'Sustainable Management'
    END AS water_resource_management_status
FROM wrmi_calc
GROUP BY stationname, locationtype
ORDER BY AVG(wrmi) DESC, AVG(waterqualityindex) DESC;

  Definition: ORS = CASE WHEN operationalstatus = 'Active' THEN 10 * (1 - (operationhours) / (maintenancecyclehours)) WHEN operationalstatus = 'Standby' THEN 5 * (1 - (operationhours) / (maintenancecyclehours)) ELSE 0 END
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT

  operationhours,
  maintenancecyclehours,
  operationalstatus,
  CASE
    WHEN operationalstatus = 'Active'
      THEN 10 * (1 - operationhours / NULLIF(maintenancecyclehours, 0))
    WHEN operationalstatus = 'Standby'
      THEN 5 * (1 - operationhours / NULLIF(maintenancecyclehours, 0))

  END AS ors
FROM operationmaintenance;

I would like to assess our polar base communication systems by calculating the Base Station Communication Stability Index for each communication unit. Please extract the registry ID, antenna status, radio signal strength, and network latency from our communication records, then calculate both the Communication Reliability Index and BSCSI for each unit. Make sure to round all values to two decimal places for clarity in reporting.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Communication Reliability Index (CRI): Assesses the reliability of communication systems based on signal metrics and antenna status.
  Definition: CRI = CASE WHEN antennastatus = 'Error' THEN 0 WHEN antennastatus = 'Warning' THEN 5 WHEN antennastatus = 'Normal' THEN 10 ELSE 0 END * (1 - (signalmetrics.latency_ms) / (1000)), where lower latency and better antenna status result in higher reliability.
- Base Station Communication Stability Index (BSCSI): Evaluates the stability and reliability of polar base station communication systems
  Definition: BSCSI = CRI * (1 + 0.2 * signalmetrics.radio_strength_dbm / 100) * (1 - 0.01 * (1000 - signalmetrics.latency_ms))
</definitions>

<task>
I would like to assess our polar base communication systems by calculating the Base Station Communication Stability Index for each communication unit. Please extract the registry ID, antenna status, radio signal strength, and network latency from our communication records, then calculate both the Communication Reliability Index and BSCSI for each unit. Make sure to round all values to two decimal places for clarity in reporting.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Communication Reliability Index (CRI): Assesses the reliability of communication systems based on signal metrics and antenna status.
  Definition: CRI = CASE WHEN antennastatus = 'Error' THEN 0 WHEN antennastatus = 'Warning' THEN 5 WHEN antennastatus = 'Normal' THEN 10 ELSE 0 END * (1 - (signalmetrics.latency_ms) / (1000)), where lower latency and better antenna status result in higher reliability.
- Base Station Communication Stability Index (BSCSI): Evaluates the stability and reliability of polar base station communication systems
  Definition: BSCSI = CRI * (1 + 0.2 * signalmetrics.radio_strength_dbm / 100) * (1 - 0.01 * (1000 - signalmetrics.latency_ms))
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH comm AS (
  SELECT
    c.commregistry,
    c.antennastatus,
    CAST(json_extract(c.signalmetrics, '$.radio_strength_dbm') AS REAL) AS radio_strength_dbm,
    CAST(json_extract(c.signalmetrics, '$.latency_ms') AS REAL) AS latency_ms,
    CASE
      WHEN TRIM(c.antennastatus) = 'Error' THEN 0
      WHEN TRIM(c.antennastatus) = 'Warning' THEN 5
      WHEN TRIM(c.antennastatus) = 'Normal' THEN 10
      ELSE 0
    END * (1 - CAST(json_extract(c.signalmetrics, '$.latency_ms') AS REAL) / NULLIF(1000, 0)) AS cri
  FROM communication AS c
)
SELECT
  comm.commregistry,
  comm.antennastatus,
  ROUND(comm.radio_strength_dbm, 2) AS radio_strength_dbm,
  ROUND(comm.latency_ms, 2) AS latency_ms,
  ROUND(comm.cri, 2) AS communication_reliability_index,
  ROUND(
    comm.cri * (1 + 0.2 * comm.radio_strength_dbm / NULLIF(100, 0)) * (1 - 0.01 * (1000 - comm.latency_ms)),
    2
  ) AS bscsi
FROM comm;

<domain_knowledge>
- Scientific equipment ready for measurement (SERM): Scientific equipment is operating, logging data, with normal sensors and valid calibration. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: scientificequipmentstatus = 'Operating' AND dataloggingstatus = 'Active' AND sensorstatus = 'Normal' AND calibrationstatus = 'Valid'
- Generation-to-load power ratio (GLR): Total wind, solar, and fuel-cell generation per watt of battery consumption.
  Definition: (thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.wind.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.solar.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.fuelcelloutputw) / powerbattery.powerconsumptionw
- Solar panel fault at Antarctic station (SPFAS): Solar panel fault occurring on equipment located in Antarctica.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.solarpanelstatus) = 'Fault' AND TRIM(location.locationtype) = 'Antarctic'
- Wind turbine fault at high altitude (WTFHA): Wind turbine fault recorded on equipment located above 3000 meters.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.windturbinestatus) = 'Fault' AND location.altitudem > 3000
- Active logging with high latency: Active data logging on equipment with latency above 1000 milliseconds.

<domain_knowledge>
- Scientific equipment ready for measurement (SERM): Scientific equipment is operating, logging data, with normal sensors and valid calibration. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: scientificequipmentstatus = 'Operating' AND dataloggingstatus = 'Active' AND sensorstatus = 'Normal' AND calibrationstatus = 'Valid'
- Generation-to-load power ratio (GLR): Total wind, solar, and fuel-cell generation per watt of battery consumption.
  Definition: (thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.wind.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.solar.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.fuelcelloutputw) / powerbattery.powerconsumptionw
- Solar panel fault at Antarctic station (SPFAS): Solar panel fault occurring on equipment located in Antarctica.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.solarpanelstatus) = 'Fault' AND TRIM(location.locationtype) = 'Antarctic'
- Wind turbine fault at high altitude (WTFHA): Wind turbine fault recorded on equipment located above 3000 meters.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.windturbinestatus) = 'Fault' AND location.altitudem > 3000
- Active logging with high latency: Active data logging on equipment with latency above 1000 milliseconds.
  Definition: TRIM(scientific.dataloggingstatus) = 'Active' AND communication.json_extract(signalmetrics, '$.latency_ms') > 1000
- Failed communication equipment inspection: Communication equipment whose inspection result is Failed.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.inspectionstatus) = 'Failed' AND TRIM(equipment.equipmenttype) = 'Communication'
- Non-compliant equipment with high engine temperature: Non-compliant equipment with engine temperature above 130 degrees Celsius.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.compliancestatus) = 'Non-compliant' AND engineandfluids.enginetemperaturec > 130
- Active equipment with antenna error: Active equipment whose communication antenna is in Error state.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.operationalstatus) = 'Active' AND TRIM(communication.antennastatus) = 'Error'
- Power-to-load ratio (PLR): Battery power draw per kilogram of vehicle load.
  Definition: powerbattery.powerconsumptionw / chassisandvehicle.vehicleloadkg
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
I want to calculate the Energy Sustainability Index (ESI) for equipment with an efficiency of 0.8 and energy source of 'Solar'. Please compute the ESI using the standard formula that multiplies efficiency by the appropriate source weight factor (Solar=1.5, Wind=1.5, Hybrid=1.2, Battery=1.0, Diesel=0.7, default=0) and return the result as 'esi'. Since SQLite doesn't support custom functions, implement this as a direct calculation that applies the source-based multiplier logic using a CASE expression.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Energy Sustainability Index (ESI): Measures the sustainability of an equipment's energy usage by evaluating energy efficiency and renewable sources.
  Definition: ESI = energyefficiencypercent * CASE WHEN powersource IN ('Solar', 'Wind') THEN 1.5 WHEN powersource = 'Hybrid' THEN 1.2 WHEN powersource = 'Battery' THEN 1.0 WHEN powersource = 'Diesel' THEN 0.7 ELSE 0 END, providing higher ratings for renewable energy and lower ratings for fossil fuels.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT p.energyefficiencypercent *
       CASE
           WHEN p.powersource IN ('Solar', 'Wind') THEN 1.5
           WHEN p.powersource = 'Hybrid' THEN 1.2
           WHEN p.powersource = 'Battery' THEN 1.0
           WHEN p.powersource = 'Diesel' THEN 0.7
           ELSE 0
       END AS esi
FROM powerbattery p
JOIN equipment e ON p.pwrbatteqref = e.equipmentcode
WHERE e.efficiencyindex = 0.8
  AND p.powersource = 'Solar';

instances.question:
Increase the reliability index by 15% for all equipment associated with cabins that meet our Cabin Habitability Standard.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Cabin Habitability Standard: Defines the minimum standards for habitable cabin conditions in polar environments.
  Definition: A cabin meets 'Habitability Standards' when it maintains internal temperature (cabinclimate.temperature_c) between 18-24°C, oxygen levels (cabinclimate.o2_percent) above 19.5%, CO2 levels (cabinclimate.co2_ppm) below 1000 ppm, functioning ventilation systems, and operational heating systems.
</definitions>

UPDATE equipment
SET reliabilityindex = reliabilityindex * 1.15
WHERE EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM cabinenvironment AS c
     WHERE c.cabineqref = equipment.equipmentcode
       AND json_extract(c.cabinclimate, '$.temperature_c') BETWEEN 18 AND 24
       AND json_extract(c.cabinclimate, '$.o2_percent') > 19.5
       AND json_extract(c.cabinclimate, '$.co2_ppm') < 1000
       AND TRIM(c.ventilationstatus) IN ('Auto',
                                         'On')
       AND TRIM(c.heaterstatus) IN ('Auto',
                                    'On'));

<task>
Increase the reliability index by 15% for all equipment associated with cabins that meet our Cabin Habitability Standard.
<definitions> MUST USE

  Definition: A cabin meets 'Habitability Standards' when it maintains internal temperature (cabinclimate.temperature_c) between 18-24°C, oxygen levels (cabinclimate.o2_percent) above 19.5%, CO2 levels (cabinclimate.co2_ppm) below 1000 ppm, functioning ventilation systems, and operational heating systems.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

UPDATE equipment
SET reliabilityindex = reliabilityindex * 1.15
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM cabinenvironment AS c
    WHERE c.cabineqref = equipment.equipmentcode
      AND json_extract(c.cabinclimate, '$.temperature_c') BETWEEN 18 AND 24
      AND json_extract(c.cabinclimate, '$.o2_percent') > 19.5
      AND json_extract(c.cabinclimate, '$.co2_ppm') < 1000
      AND TRIM(c.ventilationstatus) IN ('Auto', 'On')

);

Create a dashboard view called 'water_management_view' that calculates the Water Resource Management Index for all equipment with water level data. The view should display the equipment reference, the calculated WRMI value, and categorize each item according to the Water Resource Management Status Classification.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Water Resource Management Index (WRMI): Evaluates the efficiency of water resource management based on water levels, quality, and waste levels.
  Definition: WRMI = waterlevelpercent * (waterqualityindex) / (100) * (1 - (wastetanklevelpercent) / (100)), where higher water quality and appropriate water/waste levels indicate better management.
- Water Resource Management Status Classification (WRMSC): A comprehensive classification system that categorizes water resource management status based on WRMI values to guide operational decisions.
  Definition: Water management operations are classified into three status levels: 'Conservation Needed' WHEN (WRMI < 0.5), indicating critical resource limitations requiring immediate conservation measures; 'Monitoring Advised' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.5 AND WRMI < 0.7), representing adequate but vigilant management requiring regular system monitoring; 'Sustainable Management' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.7), indicating optimal water resource utilization suitable for unrestricted operations.
- Water Conservation Requirement: Specifies the conditions under which water conservation measures must be implemented.
  Definition: Water conservation measures must be implemented when the WRMI falls below 0.5, indicating either low water levels, poor water quality, or high waste tank levels that require immediate attention to maintain sustainable water usage.
</definitions>

candidates:
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS water_management_view AS
SELECT watereqref,
       wrmi,
       CASE
           WHEN wrmi < 0.5 THEN 'Conservation Needed'
           WHEN wrmi < 0.7 THEN 'Monitoring Advised'
           ELSE 'Sustainable Management'
       END AS water_resource_management_status_classification
FROM
  (SELECT watereqref,
          CAST(waterlevelpercent AS REAL) * (CAST(waterqualityindex AS REAL) / NULLIF(100, 0)) * (1.0 - CAST(wastetanklevelpercent AS REAL) / NULLIF(100, 0)) AS wrmi
   FROM waterandwaste);

<task>
Create a dashboard view called 'water_management_view' that calculates the Water Resource Management Index for all equipment with water level data. The view should display the equipment reference, the calculated WRMI value, and categorize each item according to the Water Resource Management Status Classification.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Water Resource Management Index (WRMI): Evaluates the efficiency of water resource management based on water levels, quality, and waste levels.
  Definition: WRMI = waterlevelpercent * (waterqualityindex) / (100) * (1 - (wastetanklevelpercent) / (100)), where higher water quality and appropriate water/waste levels indicate better management.
- Water Resource Management Status Classification (WRMSC): A comprehensive classification system that categorizes water resource management status based on WRMI values to guide operational decisions.
  Definition: Water management operations are classified into three status levels: 'Conservation Needed' WHEN (WRMI < 0.5), indicating critical resource limitations requiring immediate conservation measures; 'Monitoring Advised' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.5 AND WRMI < 0.7), representing adequate but vigilant management requiring regular system monitoring; 'Sustainable Management' WHEN (WRMI >= 0.7), indicating optimal water resource utilization suitable for unrestricted operations.
- Water Conservation Requirement: Specifies the conditions under which water conservation measures must be implemented.
  Definition: Water conservation measures must be implemented when the WRMI falls below 0.5, indicating either low water levels, poor water quality, or high waste tank levels that require immediate attention to maintain sustainable water usage.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS water_management_view AS
SELECT
  watereqref,
  wrmi,
  CASE
    WHEN wrmi < 0.5 THEN 'Conservation Needed'
    WHEN wrmi < 0.7 THEN 'Monitoring Advised'
    ELSE 'Sustainable Management'
  END AS water_resource_management_status_classification
FROM (
  SELECT
    watereqref,
    CAST(waterlevelpercent AS REAL) * (CAST(waterqualityindex AS REAL) / NULLIF(100, 0)) * (1.0 - CAST(wastetanklevelpercent AS REAL) / NULLIF(100, 0)) AS wrmi
  FROM waterandwaste
);

For our polar vehicles, we need to calculate the Vehicle Performance Coefficient (VPC) for a specific vehicle with the following parameters: brake pad wear of 20%, track wear of 30%, vehicle speed of 40 km/h, and engine load of 80%. Please compute the VPC using the standard formula with input validation that checks if brake wear and track wear are between 0-100%, vehicle speed is non-negative, and engine load is between 0-100%. Return NULL if any validation fails, otherwise calculate the VPC using the formula: (1 - (brake_wear + track_wear)/200) * (vehicle_speed/50) * (engine_load/100), and return the result as 'vpc_result'.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Vehicle Performance Coefficient (VPC): A metric that evaluates vehicle performance based on mechanical condition and operational efficiency.
  Definition: VPC = (1 - (brakepadwearpercent + trackwearpercent) / (200)) * (vehiclespeedkmh) / (50) * (engineloadpercent) / (100), where lower wear percentages and optimal engine load contribute to better performance.
</definitions>

<domain_knowledge>
- Scientific equipment ready for measurement (SERM): Scientific equipment is operating, logging data, with normal sensors and valid calibration. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: scientificequipmentstatus = 'Operating' AND dataloggingstatus = 'Active' AND sensorstatus = 'Normal' AND calibrationstatus = 'Valid'
- Generation-to-load power ratio (GLR): Total wind, solar, and fuel-cell generation per watt of battery consumption.
  Definition: (thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.wind.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.json_extract(renewablemetrics, '$.solar.output_w') + thermalsolarwindandgrid.fuelcelloutputw) / powerbattery.powerconsumptionw
- Solar panel fault at Antarctic station (SPFAS): Solar panel fault occurring on equipment located in Antarctica.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.solarpanelstatus) = 'Fault' AND TRIM(location.locationtype) = 'Antarctic'
- Wind turbine fault at high altitude (WTFHA): Wind turbine fault recorded on equipment located above 3000 meters.
  Definition: TRIM(thermalsolarwindandgrid.windturbinestatus) = 'Fault' AND location.altitudem > 3000
- Active logging with high latency: Active data logging on equipment with latency above 1000 milliseconds.
  Definition: TRIM(scientific.dataloggingstatus) = 'Active' AND communication.json_extract(signalmetrics, '$.latency_ms') > 1000
- Failed communication equipment inspection: Communication equipment whose inspection result is Failed.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.inspectionstatus) = 'Failed' AND TRIM(equipment.equipmenttype) = 'Communication'
- Non-compliant equipment with high engine temperature: Non-compliant equipment with engine temperature above 130 degrees Celsius.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.compliancestatus) = 'Non-compliant' AND engineandfluids.enginetemperaturec > 130
- Active equipment with antenna error: Active equipment whose communication antenna is in Error state.
  Definition: TRIM(operationmaintenance.operationalstatus) = 'Active' AND TRIM(communication.antennastatus) = 'Error'
- Power-to-load ratio (PLR): Battery power draw per kilogram of vehicle load.
  Definition: powerbattery.powerconsumptionw / chassisandvehicle.vehicleloadkg
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
For our polar vehicles, we need to calculate the Vehicle Performance Coefficient (VPC) for a specific vehicle with the following parameters: brake pad wear of 20%, track wear of 30%, vehicle speed of 40 km/h, and engine load of 80%. Please compute the VPC using the standard formula with input validation that checks if brake wear and track wear are between 0-100%, vehicle speed is non-negative, and engine load is between 0-100%. Return NULL if any validation fails, otherwise calculate the VPC using the formula: (1 - (brake_wear + track_wear)/200) * (vehicle_speed/50) * (engine_load/100), and return the result as 'vpc_result'.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Vehicle Performance Coefficient (VPC): A metric that evaluates vehicle performance based on mechanical condition and operational efficiency.
  Definition: VPC = (1 - (brakepadwearpercent + trackwearpercent) / (200)) * (vehiclespeedkmh) / (50) * (engineloadpercent) / (100), where lower wear percentages and optimal engine load contribute to better performance.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH params(brake_wear, track_wear, vehicle_speed, engine_load) AS (
  SELECT 20, 30, 40, 80
)
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN brake_wear BETWEEN 0 AND 100
     AND track_wear BETWEEN 0 AND 100
     AND vehicle_speed >= 0
     AND engine_load BETWEEN 0 AND 100
    THEN (1 - CAST((brake_wear + track_wear) AS REAL) / NULLIF(200, 0))
         * (CAST(vehicle_speed AS REAL) / NULLIF(50, 0))
         * (CAST(engine_load AS REAL) / NULLIF(100, 0))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS vpc_result
FROM params;

Identify robots with a High Safety Concern and a High Fault Risk based on their most recent maintenance record. List the robot ID, Safety Incident Score (SIS), and the recent fault prediction score. Sort the results by SIS in descending order and limit to 100 rows.
<definitions> MUST USE
- High Fault Risk: Indicates if the robot has a high risk of fault based on average fault prediction score.

<domain_knowledge>
- Total motor power (Ptotal): Total electrical power consumed by all six motors.
  Definition: m1currval * m1voltval + m2currval * m2voltval + m3currval * m3voltval + m4currval * m4voltval + m5currval * m5voltval + m6currval * m6voltval
- High average joint temperature articulated robot: Articulated robot whose average joint temperature exceeds 70.
  Definition: (j1tempval + j2tempval + j3tempval + j4tempval + j5tempval + j6tempval) / 6 > 70 AND TRIM(bottypeval) = 'Articulated'
- High average joint vibration collaborative robot: Collaborative robot whose average joint vibration exceeds 8.
  Definition: (j1vibval + j2vibval + j3vibval + j4vibval + j5vibval + j6vibval) / 6 > 8 AND TRIM(bottypeval) = 'Collaborative'
- High average joint backlash delta robot: Delta robot whose average joint backlash exceeds 0.08 millimeters.
  Definition: (j1backval + j2backval + j3backval + j4backval + j5backval + j6backval) / 6 > 0.08 AND TRIM(bottypeval) = 'Delta'
- average joint temperature (AVG_TEMP): Mean temperature reading across the six joints.

Identify robots with a High Safety Concern and a High Fault Risk based on their most recent maintenance record. List the robot ID, Safety Incident Score (SIS), and the recent fault prediction score. Sort the results by SIS in descending order and limit to 100 rows.
<definitions> MUST USE

- Safety Incident Score (SIS): Aggregates safety incidents from JSONB safety_metrics.
  Definition: For a given robot R, SIS = SUM_ps in performance_and_safety where effectivenessrobot = R (safety_metrics->>'overloads'::int + safety_metrics->>'collisions'::int + safety_metrics->>'emergency_stops'::int + safety_metrics->>'speed_violations'::int), where JSONB fields are extracted and summed.
- High Safety Concern: Flags robots with significant safety incidents.
  Definition: A robot R has High Safety Concern if SIS > 20.
- Recent Fault Prediction Score (RFPS): The fault prediction score from the most recent maintenance record for a robot.
  Definition: For a given robot R, faultpredscore(mf) where mf in maintenance_and_fault, upkeeprobot = R, and upkeepduedays(mf) = min_mf' in maintenance_and_fault where upkeeprobot = R upkeepduedays(mf').
</definitions>
</task>

```sql
WITH safety AS (
  SELECT effectivenessrobot AS robot_id,
         SUM(
           COALESCE(CAST(json_extract(safety_metrics, '$.overloads') AS INTEGER), 0)
           + COALESCE(CAST(json_extract(safety_metrics, '$.collisions') AS INTEGER), 0)
           + COALESCE(CAST(json_extract(safety_metrics, '$.emergency_stops') AS INTEGER), 0)
           + COALESCE(CAST(json_extract(safety_metrics, '$.speed_violations') AS INTEGER), 0)
         ) AS sis
  FROM performance_and_safety
  GROUP BY effectivenessrobot
),
recent AS (
  SELECT upkeeprobot AS robot_id,
         faultpredscore AS rfps,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY upkeeprobot
           ORDER BY upkeepduedays ASC
         ) AS rn
  FROM maintenance_and_fault
)
SELECT s.robot_id,
       s.sis,
       r.rfps
FROM safety s
JOIN recent r
  ON s.robot_id = r.robot_id
WHERE r.rn = 1
  AND s.sis > 20
  AND r.rfps > 0.5
ORDER BY s.sis DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

Also, count robots with Cycle Efficiency Category of 'Low Efficiency'. Sort by average OCE from highest to lowest and limit to 50 rows.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Operation Cycle Efficiency (OCE): Calculates the efficiency of program cycles relative to cycle time.
  Definition: For a given robot R, OCE = (TPC) / (SUM_o in operation where operbotdetref = R cycletimesecval)
- Total Program Cycles (TPC): Sums the program cycle counts across all operations for a specific robot.
  Definition: For a given robot R, TPC = SUM_o in operation where operbotdetref = R progcyclecount
- Average Cycle Time: Calculates the average time in seconds for completing one program cycle
  Definition: For a given robot R, Average Cycle Time = (SUM_o in operation where operbotdetref = R cycletimesecval) / (COUNT((o in operation where operbotdetref = R)))
- Cycle Efficiency Category: Categorizes robots based on their program cycle efficiency performance
  Definition: For a robot R, the Cycle Efficiency Category is:
- 'Low Efficiency' if OCE < 100 AND TPC > 500000
- 'Medium Efficiency' if OCE < 150 OR TPC > 300000
- 'High Efficiency' otherwise
- Program Efficiency Rank: Ranks programs based on their average Operation Cycle Efficiency across robots.
  Definition: For a program P, Program Efficiency Rank = DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(program_oce) DESC), where program_oce is the Operation Cycle Efficiency for program P on each robot.
- Efficiency Metrics: Aggregates efficiency-related metrics, including the most efficient program and average program Operation Cycle Efficiency.
  Definition: For a model series, Efficiency Metrics = jsonb_build_object('most_efficient_program', currprogval with Program Efficiency Rank = 1, 'avg_program_efficiency', AVG(avg_program_oce)), where avg_program_oce is the average Operation Cycle Efficiency per program.
</definitions>

<task>
I want to analyze robot efficiency by model series, focusing on Operation Cycle Efficiency, Total Program Cycles, and Average Cycle Time. For each model series with at least 5 robots, list the model series name, number of robots, average OCE and average number of programs per robot rounded to 2 decimal place, average TPC, and Efficiency Metrics as a JSON object containing the most efficient program (by Program Efficiency Rank) and the average OCE across all programs. Also, count robots with Cycle Efficiency Category of 'Low Efficiency'. Sort by average OCE from highest to lowest and limit to 50 rows.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Operation Cycle Efficiency (OCE): Calculates the efficiency of program cycles relative to cycle time.
  Definition: For a given robot R, OCE = (TPC) / (SUM_o in operation where operbotdetref = R cycletimesecval)
- Total Program Cycles (TPC): Sums the program cycle counts across all operations for a specific robot.
  Definition: For a given robot R, TPC = SUM_o in operation where operbotdetref = R progcyclecount
- Average Cycle Time: Calculates the average time in seconds for completing one program cycle
  Definition: For a given robot R, Average Cycle Time = (SUM_o in operation where operbotdetref = R cycletimesecval) / (COUNT((o in operation where operbotdetref = R)))
- Cycle Efficiency Category: Categorizes robots based on their program cycle efficiency performance
  Definition: For a robot R, the Cycle Efficiency Category is:
- 'Low Efficiency' if OCE < 100 AND TPC > 500000
- 'Medium Efficiency' if OCE < 150 OR TPC > 300000
- 'High Efficiency' otherwise
- Program Efficiency Rank: Ranks programs based on their average Operation Cycle Efficiency across robots.
  Definition: For a program P, Program Efficiency Rank = DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(program_oce) DESC), where program_oce is the Operation Cycle Efficiency for program P on each robot.
- Efficiency Metrics: Aggregates efficiency-related metrics, including the most efficient program and average program Operation Cycle Efficiency.
  Definition: For a model series, Efficiency Metrics = jsonb_build_object('most_efficient_program', currprogval with Program Efficiency Rank = 1, 'avg_program_efficiency', AVG(avg_program_oce)), where avg_program_oce is the average Operation Cycle Efficiency per program.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH op_prog AS (
    SELECT
        o.operbotdetref AS botdetreg,
        o.currprogval,
        CAST(SUM(o.progcyclecount) AS REAL) / NULLIF(SUM(o.cycletimesecval), 0) AS program_oce
    FROM operation o
    GROUP BY o.operbotdetref, o.currprogval
),
program_ranks AS (
    SELECT
        currprogval,
        AVG(program_oce) AS avg_program_oce,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(program_oce) DESC) AS program_eff_rank
    FROM op_prog
    GROUP BY currprogval
),
robot_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        rd.botdetreg,
        rd.modelseriesval,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.currprogval) AS num_programs,
        SUM(o.progcyclecount) AS tpc,
        CAST(SUM(o.progcyclecount) AS REAL) / NULLIF(SUM(o.cycletimesecval), 0) AS oce,
        CASE
            WHEN CAST(SUM(o.progcyclecount) AS REAL) / NULLIF(SUM(o.cycletimesecval), 0) < 100
                 AND SUM(o.progcyclecount) > 500000 THEN 'Low Efficiency'
            WHEN CAST(SUM(o.progcyclecount) AS REAL) / NULLIF(SUM(o.cycletimesecval), 0) < 150
                 OR SUM(o.progcyclecount) > 300000 THEN 'Medium Efficiency'
            ELSE 'High Efficiency'
        END AS efficiency_category
    FROM robot_details rd
    JOIN operation o ON o.operbotdetref = rd.botdetreg
    GROUP BY rd.botdetreg, rd.modelseriesval
),
series_agg AS (
    SELECT
        modelseriesval,
        COUNT(DISTINCT botdetreg) AS num_robots,
        AVG(oce) AS avg_oce_raw,
        AVG(num_programs) AS avg_num_programs_raw,
        AVG(tpc) AS avg_tpc,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN efficiency_category = 'Low Efficiency' THEN 1 END) AS low_efficiency_count
    FROM robot_metrics
    GROUP BY modelseriesval
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT botdetreg) >= 5
),
series_programs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        rd.modelseriesval,
        op.currprogval
    FROM robot_details rd
    JOIN op_prog op ON rd.botdetreg = op.botdetreg
),
series_eff AS (
    SELECT
        sp.modelseriesval,
        AVG(pr.avg_program_oce) AS avg_program_efficiency
    FROM series_programs sp
    JOIN program_ranks pr ON sp.currprogval = pr.currprogval
    GROUP BY sp.modelseriesval
),
best_program AS (
    SELECT modelseriesval, currprogval
    FROM (
        SELECT
            sp.modelseriesval,
            sp.currprogval,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY sp.modelseriesval
                ORDER BY pr.program_eff_rank ASC, sp.currprogval ASC
            ) AS rn
        FROM series_programs sp
        JOIN program_ranks pr ON sp.currprogval = pr.currprogval
    ) t
    WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
    sa.modelseriesval,
    sa.num_robots,
    ROUND(sa.avg_oce_raw, 2) AS avg_oce,
    ROUND(sa.avg_num_programs_raw, 2) AS avg_num_programs_per_robot,
    sa.avg_tpc,
    json_object(
        'most_efficient_program', bp.currprogval,
        'avg_program_efficiency', se.avg_program_efficiency
    ) AS efficiency_metrics,
    sa.low_efficiency_count
FROM series_agg sa
LEFT JOIN best_program bp ON sa.modelseriesval = bp.modelseriesval
LEFT JOIN series_eff se ON sa.modelseriesval = se.modelseriesval
ORDER BY sa.avg_oce_raw DESC
LIMIT 50;

instances.question:
I want to analyze the relationship between Joint Degradation Index and Total Operating Hours for robots with Joint Health Risk. Please list each robot's ID, its JDI, Maximum Joint Temperature, TOH, and the regression slope of JDI versus TOH across all qualifying robots. Sort the results by JDI from highest to lowest, and limit the output to 100 rows.
<definitions> MUST USE
- JDI-TOH Regression Slope: Measures the linear relationship between Joint Degradation Index and Total Operating Hours using regression.
  Definition: For a set of robots meeting JDI > 1.5, MJT > 65, and TOH > 5000, the JDI-TOH Regression Slope is given by [ slope = (n SUM (x_i y_i) - SUM x_i SUM y_i) / (n SUM POWER(x_i, 2) - (SUM x_i)^2) ] where ( y_i = JDI ) (Joint Degradation Index for robot ( i )), ( x_i = TOH ) (Total Operating Hours for robot ( i )), ( n ) is the number of qualifying robots, and sums are over all qualifying robots.
- Joint Degradation Index (JDI): Computes a composite index of joint health based on temperature and vibration.
  Definition: For a given robot R, JDI = (SUM_jc in joint_condition where jcdetref = R SUM_i=POWER(1, 6) (jitempval_i / MJT + jivibval_i)) / (COUNT((jc in joint_condition where jcdetref = R)) * 6), where MJT normalizes temperatures, and jitempval_i, jivibval_i are joint i's temperature and vibration.
- Total Operating Hours (TOH): The maximum total operating hours recorded for the robot across all operations.
  Definition: For a given robot R, TOH = max_o in operation where operbotdetref = R totopshrval
- Maximum Joint Temperature (MJT): Finds the maximum temperature recorded for any joint across all operations for a specific robot.
  Definition: For a given robot R, MJT = max_jc in joint_condition where jcdetref = R max(jc.j1tempval, jc.j2tempval, jc.j3tempval, jc.j4tempval, jc.j5tempval, jc.j6tempval)
- Joint Health Risk: Indicates robots at risk of joint failure.
  Definition: A robot R has Joint Health Risk if JDI > 1.5 and MJT > 65.
</definitions>

candidates:
WITH robot_base AS
  (SELECT rd.botdetreg,

     (SELECT MAX(MAX(jc.j1tempval, jc.j2tempval, jc.j3tempval, jc.j4tempval, jc.j5tempval, jc.j6tempval))
      FROM joint_condition jc
      WHERE jc.jcdetref = rd.botdetreg) AS mjt,

     (SELECT MAX(op.totopshrval)
      FROM OPERATION op
      WHERE op.operbotdetref = rd.botdetreg) AS toh
   FROM robot_details rd),
     robot_jdi AS
  (SELECT rb.botdetreg,
          rb.mjt,
          rb.toh,
          SUM(CAST((jc.j1tempval + jc.j2tempval + jc.j3tempval + jc.j4tempval + jc.j5tempval + jc.j6tempval) AS REAL) / NULLIF(rb.mjt, 0) + (jc.j1vibval + jc.j2vibval + jc.j3vibval + jc.j4vibval + jc.j5vibval + jc.j6vibval)) / (COUNT(*) * 6.0) AS jdi
   FROM robot_base rb
   JOIN joint_condition jc ON jc.jcdetref = rb.botdetreg
   GROUP BY rb.botdetreg,
            rb.mjt,
            rb.toh),
     regression_stats AS
  (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n,
          SUM(toh) AS sum_x,
          SUM(jdi) AS sum_y,
          SUM(toh * jdi) AS sum_xy,
          SUM(toh * toh) AS sum_x2
   FROM robot_jdi
   WHERE jdi > 1.5
     AND mjt > 65
     AND toh > 5000)
SELECT rj.botdetreg,
       rj.jdi,
       rj.mjt AS maximum_joint_temperature,
       rj.toh,
       CAST((rs.n * rs.sum_xy - rs.sum_x * rs.sum_y) AS REAL) / NULLIF((rs.n * rs.sum_x2 - rs.sum_x * rs.sum_x), 0) AS jdi_toh_regression_slope
FROM robot_jdi rj
JOIN regression_stats rs ON 1 = 1
WHERE rj.jdi > 1.5
  AND rj.mjt > 65
  AND rj.toh > 5000
ORDER BY rj.jdi DESC
LIMIT 100;
